role: E04 controlled-reconstruction geometry substitute: 3DMM fitting -> dense mesh -> Q=140 vertices -> depth target M0
authorization: Owner decision M6A5b: E04-2 = OPTION B (CONTROLLED_ADAPTATION). Task section 2.1 authorises model-asset download for the chosen E04 geometry substitute after provenance is established.

selection.why_not_tier_A: Tier A (the paper's own [61] Dense Face Alignment with a legally obtained BFM) is not reproducible: the [61] release is MATLAB/MatConvNet TEST-ONLY code and requires the registration-gated Basel Face Model, which cannot be acquired programmatically and must not be redistributed.

rejected_alternatives.reason: MATLAB/MatConvNet test-only; BFM registration-gated; not a reproducible executable route.

Apache-2.0 and fully public, but it is a LANDMARK REGRESSOR with a fixed 468-vertex topology, NOT a morphable model. It has no shape/expression basis, so it cannot perform the paper's stated 'fit a 3DMM model' role. Rejected on closeness-to-paper grounds, not on convenience.
FLAME is registration-gated like BFM, so the reproducibility problem is unchanged; FLAME is also a different model family from the paper's BFM lineage.

why_chosen: It performs the paper's exact function: fits a 3DMM (shape basis + expression basis + weak-perspective pose) and produces a DENSE 3D mesh, as recon_vers(dense_flag=True) shows.
Its model IS a BFM2009 derivative - the SAME model family the paper's [61] requires - so the substitution stays inside the paper's 3DMM lineage.
It ships its own official depth renderer (utils/depth.py + Sim3DR z-buffer), so the depth semantics are taken from an authoritative implementation rather than invented by this benchmark.
It carries its own 68 iBUG landmark vertex correspondence (keypoints), giving semantic anchors for the Q=140 rule without any manual selection.
Deterministic inference: a single feed-forward regressor with fixed parameter mean/std, no sampling, no iterative optimisation.
Stable vertex indexing: a fixed 38,365-vertex topology with a fixed 76,073-triangle triangulation, identical for every image.
Licence position is recorded factually under model_asset_license; this benchmark offers no independent legal interpretation.

model_geometry.landmark_correspondence: 68 iBUG keypoints carried by the model (keypoints array, 204 = 68*3 flat indices)
model_geometry.known_upstream_quirk: keypoints row 44 is [37149, 37150, 36263] - its z component indexes a DIFFERENT vertex (36263//3 = 12087) than its x/y (12383). The E04 contract therefore derives anchor vertex ids with the consistent x-component rule keypoints.reshape(68,3)[:,0]//3. Disclosed, not silently ignored.

capability_verification.method: synthetic 3DMM parameters (alpha_shp = alpha_exp = 0, synthetic frontal pose); no benchmark image was read
capability_verification.projected_vertices: VERIFIED - official similar_transform() maps the mesh into the canonical 256 frame
capability_verification.depth: VERIFIED - z-buffer rasterisation then INTER_AREA resize produced a 32x32 map in [0,1] with background 0 and a clear face-like central ridge
capability_verification.note: Numpy was used to reproduce the official Sim3DR z-buffer semantics because torch and the Sim3DR Cython extension are not installed in this audit environment. The AUTHORITATIVE runtime renderer remains the official Sim3DR at the pinned commit.
